content.title: About
content.content: Celery is a perennial herbaceous plant of the Apiaceae family cultivated for its crunchy stalks, leaves, and seeds. Raw celery has a crisp texture, mildly bitter, refreshing flavor and very low calorie content. It is used in fresh salads, juices, soups, and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Celery belongs to the same family as carrots, parsley, and dill.
Celery was known in ancient Egypt, where it was used for medicinal purposes.
Celery contains natural phytochemicals called phthalides that may help lower blood pressure.
Celery stalks can grow up to 30 cm long, while the leaf blades can reach 60 cm in width.
Celery is often featured in detox diets because of its diuretic properties.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Raw celery provides about 16 kcal per 100 g, making it an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamins A and C
items.content: These antioxidants support immune function, vision, and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phytochemical compounds
items.content: Phthalides and flavonoids may contribute to lower blood pressure and improved cardiovascular function.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to celery, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Celery can enhance the effects of anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin) due to its high vitamin K content.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: As with many vegetables, celery may carry pesticide residues; thorough washing before consumption is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw celery can be eaten as a snack, cut into sticks for dips, added to salads, smoothies, and juices. It also serves as an aromatic base for soups and stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store celery in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a damp towel or in a perforated plastic bag. When stored properly it stays fresh for up to 2 weeks. Remove any yellowing leaves.
